---
title: "Create your personal workspace"
---

You only need to perform the complete procedure on this page once.

## 1. Create or sign in to your GitHub account

[GitHub](https://github.com/) is a collaborative platform built around
**repositories**: project spaces in which files can be stored, their changes can
be tracked, and work can be shared with other people. It is widely used for
software development, but also by researchers and students who write scripts or
notebooks for data analysis, numerical modelling, reproducible research, and
thesis projects. You may therefore encounter GitHub again well beyond this
laboratory.

For Mineral Science, GitHub has two practical roles:

1. it stores the permanent private repository containing your laboratory work;
2. it provides access to **GitHub Codespaces**, the remote Linux environment in
   which you will run the notebooks.

::: {.callout-note}
## Four terms that will appear repeatedly

| Term | Meaning in this course |
|---|---|
| **GitHub account** | Your personal identity on GitHub |
| **Repository** | The online project containing files and their version history |
| **Template repository** | The instructor-provided starting point from which you create your own repository |
| **Codespace** | A remote Linux computer, opened in the browser, connected to your repository |
:::

You do not need previous experience with Git or software development. During the
course you will use only a small and well-defined subset of GitHub features.

### If you already have a GitHub account

Open [GitHub](https://github.com/) and sign in with your personal account, then
continue with the Codespaces setting below.

### If you do not yet have a GitHub account

1. Open <https://github.com/signup>.
2. Create a **personal account** by following the instructions on the page. You
   may also be offered supported social sign-in options. A free GitHub account
   is sufficient for the course.
3. Choose a username that you will recognize later. Your username is your
   identity on GitHub, so choose something that you would also be comfortable
   using for future academic or research work.
4. Use an email address that you can access and complete the account-creation
   prompts.
5. **Verify your email address** using the message sent by GitHub. Do not skip
   this step: an unverified email prevents some basic GitHub operations,
   including creating a repository.
6. Return to <https://github.com/> and sign in. You should see your profile icon
   in the upper-right corner of the page.

GitHub also recommends enabling two-factor authentication (2FA) to protect your
account. This is good practice, although it is not required to complete the
first laboratory setup.

### Recommended Codespaces setting

Before creating your first Codespace:

1. select your profile picture in the upper-right corner of GitHub;
2. select **Settings**;
3. in the sidebar, under **Code, planning, and automation**, select
   **Codespaces**;
4. find **Default idle timeout**;
5. set it to **15 minutes** and save the setting.

This is a course recommendation. It limits unnecessary use of your Codespaces
allowance if you forget to stop a session manually. You should still stop the
Codespace explicitly whenever you finish working.

## 2. Open the workspace template

Open the course workspace repository:

<https://github.com/gfulian/mineral-science-lab-workspace>

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not fork the repository

Do **not** use **Fork** and do **not** select **Open in a codespace** directly
from the template.

You must first create your own repository from the template. This ensures that
your work is permanently connected to your own GitHub repository.
:::

## 3. Create your private repository

On the workspace template page:

1. Select **Use this template**.
2. Select **Create a new repository**.
3. Set **Owner** to your personal GitHub account.
4. Give the repository a recognizable name, for example
   `mineral-science-lab-yourname`.
5. Select **Private** visibility.
6. Leave **Include all branches** disabled.
7. Select **Create repository from template**.

You now have your own independent copy of the laboratory workspace.

Before continuing, check the top of the GitHub page. The repository should be
shown under **your own username**, and it should be marked **Private**. You
should no longer be looking at the instructor's template repository.

Keep this repository private unless the instructor explicitly asks you to
change its visibility.

## 4. Create the Codespace

From **your new private repository**:

1. Select the green **Code** button.
2. Open the **Codespaces** tab.
3. Select **Create codespace on main**.

If GitHub offers a choice of machine type, select the **2-core** machine. The
laboratory notebook work does not require a larger machine.

The first initialization can take a few minutes. This is normal: GitHub is
creating the remote Linux environment and the course setup is installing the
required scientific Python packages.

::: {.callout-note}
## Wait for the setup to finish

During the first launch, a terminal may display package installation messages.
Wait until the setup reports:

```text
Environment ready.
```

before starting to work.
:::

## 5. Check the environment

Open a terminal inside the Codespace using **Terminal → New Terminal** and run:

```bash
python -c "import gemmi, spglib, py3Dmol, quantas, numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib; print('Environment OK')"
```

The final line should be:

```text
Environment OK
```

Then check that the two course commands are available:

```bash
command -v update-course
command -v start-lab
command -v quantas
```

All three commands should return a path.

You can also inspect the top-level directories:

```bash
ls
```

You should see, among other files:

```text
course
work
```

If these checks succeed, your laboratory environment is ready.

Continue with **[Working in Codespaces](03-working-in-codespaces.qmd)**.
